Article Title: Why Indian pilots struggle to take jobs abroad
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: At a time when pilots’ mental health has emerged as a key concern post some recent events, with flydubai cockpit fight being the most recent one, India’s restrictive rules for cockpit crew to leaves domestic airlines only after serving long notice periods could be adding to their stress. The rule for a co-pilot to serve six months’ notice and a captain a year (which has been challenged legally), has made it difficult for foreign airlines to hire Indian aviators as they mostly want people to join in three months. Now with Captain Smit Machchhar proving his mettle in flydubai, the budget arm of Dubai’s mega carrier Emirates, Indian pilots hope foreign airlines — primarily in Gulf and other places like Sri Lanka and South Korea — keep the Indian reality in mind while giving them offer letters.“We usually don’t hire direct from India and prefer if a pilot has worked in a second country before onboarding them,” a senior official of a leading West Asian airline had recently told TOI. The reasons are two-fold: India’s notice period requirement, which remains binding for pilots even if the employer in India defaults on contractual obligations like paying on time, and then informal tie-ups with big Indian carriers against “poaching.A senior official of an airline here said: “Because of the notice period requirement, some pilots here give ‘fake resignation’ in advance and then look for jobs so that they can leave in three months of getting a job abroad. And if they don’t get a job, they take the fake resignation back.”The notice period rule has been challenged by pilots in court and the matter is sub judice. “There are concerns about pilots’ state of mind due to what could be going on in their personal lives. This notice period rule, meant to ensure schedule integrity of airlines by preventing sudden mass resignations, has outlived its utility. Today India has two big and well-funded airline and a few emerging ones. Now it is only protecting airlines that are unable to pay,” said a pilot.
Article Summary: India’s restrictive rules for cockpit crew to leaves domestic airlines only after serving long notice periods could be adding to their stress. The rule for a co-pilot to serve six months’ notice and a captain a year (which has been challenged legally) has made it difficult for foreign airlines to hire indian aviators.

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Friday accused the Election Commission (EC) of “lying” about its ECINet portal, alleging that the platform was not in accordance with the law.Congress MP Jairam Ramesh also questioned the "intentions" of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, describing them as “not honest.”“In its damage-control but actually damage-enhancing press note on September 26, 2026, the Election Commission of India had promised a committee to certify that the legally suspect ECINet ‘complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules’. In reality, this should never have been in doubt at all in the first place if the intentions of the CEC Gyanesh Kumar were honest—which they were not,” Ramesh wrote on X.He was referring to the poll panel’s statement last week, issued days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the previous 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which they maintained had been issued without their knowledge or recommendation.“ECINet was launched on January 22, 2026, with much fanfare to ‘enhance transparency, credibility and public trust’. The ECI press note issued that day assured the country that it ‘has been developed in strict accordance with the law’ and in full compliance with the Constitution of India, the Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951, and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960,” Ramesh wrote.“All of this was a lie,” he added.Ramesh further accused the EC of "violating" laws governing the electoral process.“By restricting Electoral Registration Officers’ (EROs) access to the ECINet voter-roll system and overruling EROs in states such as Goa and West Bengal, among others, the ECI under the CEC has violated the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has declined to meet the parliamentary committee, which is examining a Constitution amendment bill proposing simultaneous elections, saying it will not be desirable for senior judges to discuss the matter as the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review.A communication from the secretary general of the Supreme Court to the committee said the proposal for an informal discussion by the joint committee to examine Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the UT Laws (Amendments Bill, 2024) on the subject of simultaneous elections with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and other judges on Oct 6 was discussed among the senior judges.A communication from the secretary general of SC said, “They are of the opinion that as the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review before SC, it may not be expedient or desirable to discuss the issue on the administrative side. Opposition parties are critical of the bill, alleging that it is unconstitutional and violates federal rights.BJP and its allies have, however, backed the idea, saying a continuous cycle of elections hampers development, and simultaneous elections will also boost economic growth.

Article Title: Flydubai flight drama: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing plane
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An Indian pilot has been identified as the captain who helped prevent a flydubai passenger plane from crashing after his co-pilot allegedly tried to take control of the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli media reports and an Israeli journalist.The Indian pilot has been identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai, who intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it.The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports and officials.Machchhar is an experienced commercial pilot with more than 13 years of flying experience on Boeing 737 aircraft. He has been a captain with flydubai since June 2022, having previously spent 11 years with SpiceJet, where he served as a senior commander and Line Training Captain.During his time at SpiceJet, Machchhar reportedly flew more than 9,500 hours, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command, and served as a Line Training Captain from November 2020 to June 2022. His experience includes pilot training and mentoring, crew resource management, flight standards and compliance, and B737 NG and MAX operations.The incident unfolded aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 sending emergency signals before making an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The flight was carrying around 180 Israeli passengers, all of whom were reported safe.Also read: Passengers recall harrowing ordeal on flight that nearly crashed The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was flying over Jordan when it transmitted an emergency signal, followed by another signal indicating possible unlawful interference.Israeli officials said the emergency signals followed a physical altercation between the two pilots. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit. Both pilots were later hospitalised after the aircraft landed in Tabuk.Israeli media reports said the suspected attacker attempted to take control of the aircraft and force it into a descent. Passengers reportedly heard screaming and saw blood inside the cockpit.Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft plunging rapidly from around 34,000 feet to about 20,000 feet, with Reuters reporting a drop of nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the aircraft stabilised.The aircraft was initially treated as a possible hijacking, prompting Israeli fighter jets to be scrambled. The Israeli prime minister's office later said the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking.Israeli media reports have described the incident as a possible attempted suicide or deliberate crash, while Israeli officials cited by Reuters said they were assessing it as a possible attempted "terror attack". Reuters also reported that officials did not believe the incident was related to a mental-health issue.Later, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilots became involved in a physical altercation as the flight approached Israel. “During the flight as they approached the country one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot,” Netanyahu said in a video address.“Apparently he tried to crash the plane with its occupants.” Netanyahu added “almost all” passengers were Israelis, with some passengers and crew members breaking into the cockpit and subduing the attacker. “I spoke with one of the Israeli passengers. He told me that the plane went into a spin and began to dive. He told me that somehow he managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members and together they neutralized the stabbing pilot while he was trying to sabotage the aircraft’s systems,” Netanyahu said. “Another air crew that was on the plane entered the cockpit and managed to stabilize the plane,” he added. He also praised those who intervened, saying: “I salute these heroes who showed exceptional resourcefulness and courage.They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster.”Also read: Israel security minister on flydubai cockpit incident Flydubai has confirmed that Flight FZ1073 experienced an incident during its journey from Dubai to Tel Aviv and diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely."Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities. Further updates will be issued as additional confirmed details become available," the airline said.Read more: Passenger's mother says pilot tried to kill co-pilot on Flydubai flight The airline has not publicly confirmed the identities or nationalities of the pilots or provided details about what happened inside the cockpit.The investigation is continuing, with Israeli authorities examining the circumstances of the cockpit confrontation, the alleged attempt to take control of the aircraft and the security clearance given to the crew.
Article Summary: The indian pilot has been identified as captain smit machchhar, based in dubai. He intervened to stop his omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it. The captain has years of experience and was a spicejet pilot till 2022.

Article Title: 'He has good ideas': Putin lauds PM Modi's peace push to end Russia-Ukraine war
Article Text:
Putin says PM Modi ‘constantly raises’ need to end Ukraine conflict

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday lauded Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s efforts to seek an end to the Ukraine conflict, saying that he has “good ideas” for achieving a peaceful resolution."Prime Minister Narendra Modi is one of those world leaders who, despite our very good and even friendly relations, personal good relations, constantly raises the question and asks the question about putting an end to the conflict in Ukraine," Putin said.Asked about the issue at the Valdai Club forum, Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been actively working to find mutually acceptable solutions to the Ukraine conflict."He has an avid interest and very good ideas aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions. In that sense, naturally, the Prime Minister takes a neutral position but with an interest in the end of the conflict. I think it's my duty to say that directly. And we are thankful to the Prime Minister for his ideas," Putin said.Putin thanked PM Modi for his efforts and continued support for resolving the Ukraine conflict through dialogue."We are thankful for his desire to put an end to this conflict through peaceful means and as soon as possible," he added.Prime Minister Modi and Putin last met in September on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where they discussed strengthening trade ties, including the implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030, along with cooperation in infrastructure, energy, technology, defence and culture.PM Modi has repeatedly called for peace, stressing that India has maintained a principled and humanitarian approach to the Russia-Ukraine conflict."India has maintained a principled and humanitarian stance on the conflict which is equally appreciated by both President Putin and President Zelenskyy. In line with this, both the leaders spoke to me to share their perspectives on the developments related to the conflict. I reiterated India's principled and consistent stand and encouraged dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the conflict," the Prime Minister said during an interview with Japanese news outlet 'The Yomiuri Shimbun' while on a visit to the country in August.Responding to a question on India’s role in peace efforts between the two countries, Prime Minister Modi said, "I have already indicated India's willingness to support meaningful efforts aimed at achieving a peaceful resolution of the conflict. I believe, by virtue of our good relations with both sides, including key stakeholders, we can strengthen efforts dedicated to the restoration of an early and lasting peace in Ukraine. "This comes as Putin reiterated Moscow’s long-standing position that Russia has no plans to attack European countries, while warning that it would respond to any aggression with “all weapons” at its disposal.He also accused Western countries, particularly in Europe, of escalating tensions by discussing preparations for a possible war with Moscow, conducting military drills in the Baltic Sea and seizing Russian vessels.European leaders and intelligence agencies have warned that Russia could be capable of launching an attack on another country within the next few years, particularly if it emerges victorious from the war in Ukraine.
Article Summary: Putin says pm modi ‘constantly raises’ need to end ukraine conflict. Putin thanked pm modi for his efforts and continued support for resolving the ukraine conflict through dialogue. He said, “he saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals”.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump, pm modi, president droupadi murmu and israeli pm benjamin netanyahu, among others, have paid tribute to captain smit machchhar. The knife attack on smit by the co-pilot inside the cockpit had forced the flight carrying 174 people from dubai to tel aviv, israel, to make an emergency landing in tabuk in northwestern saudi arabia.

Article Title: Govt backs SCO connectivity, trade agenda but PM’s Pak visit uncertain
Article Text:
The first such visit from India to Pakistan since the 2025 Pahalgam terrorist attack highlighted how SCO, which is dominated by China and Russia, has remained insulated from India-Pakistan tensions, unlike the more modest Saarc regional framework.

NEW DELHI: India’s participation in the SCO meeting of national coordinators in Islamabad to firm up the calendar for high-level meetings has sparked speculation about whether PM Narendra Modi would travel to Pakistan for the heads of state summit next year. Modi has missed only 1 of the 7 in-person summits since India became a full member of the Eurasian bloc in 2017 but Indian officials warn his past attendance is no guarantee of a visit even for a multilateral event to Pakistan, a country India has come to describe as a serial practitioner of terrorism.A senior Indian diplomat, Alok Dimri, travelled to Pakistan this week for the national coordinators’ meeting, as first reported by TOI on Monday. The first such visit from India to Pakistan since the Pahalgam terrorist attack highlighted how the SCO, which is dominated by China and Russia, has remained insulated from India-Pakistan tensions, unlike the more modest SAARC regional framework.For a PM visit though, as official sources said, India will factor in Pakistan’s continued support for cross-border terrorism before making a final decision. The same is likely to apply for the meetings of defence and foreign ministers heading into the main summit, as India seeks tangible and irreversible action by Pakistan against cross-border terrorism to make the overall environment conducive for any substantive engagement.After the meeting this week, Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif will soon write to leaders of all member-states inviting them for the SCO heads of state summit. He had last invited Modi for the heads of government meeting in Islamabad in 2024 but India had then sent external affairs minister S Jaishankar who usually represents India in that meeting.Modi attends the meetings of the Council of Heads of State (CHS), the supreme decision-making body of the SCO which meets annually on a rotational basis in the country chairing the SCO. Pakistan assumed the chairship from Kyrgyzstan at the Bishkek summit last month.Although Modi did skip the Kazakhstan summit in 2024, India will likely weigh multiple geopolitical factors before deciding on his potential visit to Pakistan, apart from Pakistan-backed terrorism. India’s engagement with the SCO facilitates the ongoing normalisation of relations with China while preserving its strategic and longstanding ties with Russia.Ironically, counterterrorism and security cooperation is one key reason for New Delhi’s engagements with the grouping that also helps India with Central Asian connectivity and regional security in Afghanistan, while reinforcing its strategic autonomy.Additional secretary Dimri was greeted warmly in Pakistan, with an official photo showing him standing next to Pakistan deputy PM and foreign minister Ishaq Dar. Dimri said the national coordinators had finalised an agenda for common wellbeing and prosperity with focus on connectivity, trade and transit. “This programme will continue for a year and will culminate with Islamabad Summit,” he said.
Article Summary: The first such visit from india to pakistan since the 2025 pahalgam terrorist attack highlighted how sco has remained insulated from india-pakistan tensions. India’s engagement with the sco facilitates the ongoing normalisation of relations with china while preserving its strategic and longstanding ties with russia.

Article Title: ‘Fewer workers, more CM aspirants’: CM Mann takes swipe at Punjab Congress leadership crisis

NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Thursday took a swipe at the ongoing turmoil in the Congress state unit and said that even the new state president will not be able to unite the party leaders.Mann said that the Congress has fewer party workers but more leaders who aspire to become chief minister.“A new president will be appointed, but even the new president will not be able to unite the Congress leaders. After the new president comes, the fight amongst them will further intensify,” Mann said.“The Congress has fewer 'karyakartas' but more leaders who aspire to become CM, not for the well-being of the people but for satisfying their lust for power,” he added.This comes after the Congress high command replaced Amrinder Singh Raja Warring as the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) chief ahead of the Punjab assembly polls.Although Warring declined to comment on the development, he confirmed it by changing his X bio to “former Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President”.The move comes after months of infighting within the Punjab Congress, which intensified after the party high command decided on July 1 to retain Warring as the state unit chief.A section of leaders led by former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi had opposed Warring’s continuation and sought his removal. Leaders aligned with the Channi camp also stayed away from party programmes led by Warring.According to PTI, the Congress general secretary and Punjab in-charge held a series of meetings with state leaders before submitting his report to the party high command on the proposed leadership change.The high command subsequently informed Warring of its decision, party sources told PTI, adding that the Congress is now looking to appoint a leader who can bring different factions together ahead of the 2027 assembly polls.Warring had also faced criticism from sections of the party over the Congress’ electoral performance in Punjab and his leadership.In August, he defended himself against criticism over the party’s decline in the 2022 assembly elections, questioning attempts to hold him responsible for the loss.

Article Title: Full-body scanners at airports: Govt tests tech & algorithms to address privacy concerns before wider rollout
Article Text:
Govt are testing refined algorithms amid privacy concerns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's aviation security regulator is collecting data from ongoing trials of full-body scanners at Bengaluru and Cochin airports before deciding on their wider deployment, with the technology's algorithms also being refined to account for objects commonly worn by passengers in India.Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) Director General Rajesh Nirwan told reporters on Thursday that full-body scanners have been mandated at eight airports, while trials are currently being conducted at Bengaluru and Cochin. Authorities are collecting data from the trials, including the number of alarms generated, which will be assessed before a decision is taken on introducing the scanners at airports.However, Cochin is not among the eight airports where the scanners have been mandated.The deployment of full-body scanners has been delayed for years, partly due to concerns over passenger privacy. Nirwan said newer scanners are being made “image agnostic”, meaning they do not produce an actual image of the passenger but instead display a model and identify the specific part of the body where a suspicious object may have been detected, reported PTI.BCAS is also working with scanner vendors and original equipment manufacturers to refine the technology for Indian conditions, including concerns that jewellery and other commonly worn items could trigger alarms.“What we are getting today in India is based on algorithms that have been designed for foreign markets. There are certain typical things that are on the body of Indian citizens or people living in India. So, those algorithms are also being continuously refined,” Nirwan said.The data collected during the ongoing trials will be used to further refine the algorithms, he added.Meanwhile, the officials also addressed the recent Flydubai cockpit attack in which Indian pilot Smit Machchhar was injured, saying Indian aviation authorities are examining the incident and will hold internal deliberations on whether any aviation security advisory is required.Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha said the matter was under examination and any decision on an advisory would be taken after internal discussions. “... in case some advisory is to be issued, obviously we will put it up to the higher authorities for taking a decision on that,” Sinha said.The comments came a day after Flydubai flight FZ1073, flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 passengers, was diverted to Saudi Arabia after an altercation in the cockpit. Indian captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured while trying to tackle his co-pilot, and the aircraft later landed safely at Tabuk.
Article Summary: Govt are testing refined algorithms amid privacy concerns over jewellery and other commonly worn items. Officials also addressed the recent flydubai cockpit attack in which indian pilot smit machchhar was injured. Indian aviation authorities are examining the incident and will hold internal deliberations on whether any aviation security advisory is required.

Article Title: PM Modi urges UPSC to test aspirants’ motivation for joining civil services, not just academic knowledge
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the UPSC centenary celebration at Bharat Mandapam, in New Delhi on Thursday.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Emphasising that the purpose of recruitment for govt jobs should be to bring people into public service rather than public office, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday asked recruitment agencies like Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) to adopt selection parameters that not only test an aspirant's academic knowledge but also their motivation to join the civil services.Modi, while addressing UPSC's centenary celebrations here, explained that selecting individuals with the right inherent motivation makes it easier for the administration to adapt to rapidly changing public aspirations. Stating that the youths recruited today will simultaneously serve as the chief architects and the primary beneficiaries of the nation's future, he insisted that every selection process be rigorously tested against the dual criteria of prioritizing the nation and the citizen.Modi said the archaic 'mai-baap' (supremacy) governance mindset of the past has made way for a modern administrative era built on the absolute principle of 'nagrik devo bhava' or 'citizen is king". Projecting India as an increasingly urbanized nation by 2047 with a narrowing rural-urban divide, he said the traditional service delivery models will need to evolve to match the speed of an instant-delivery world where citizens demand rapid, real-time solutions powered by AI.“This changing mindset demands new changes from our civil services as well,” noted Modi.He demanded that selection processes for govt jobs at both national and state levels be meticulously designed to recruit professionals who proactively anticipate problems and operate without unnecessary pressure or influence. He emphasized the need for empathetic civil servants who find innovative solutions, proactively ease citizens' lives, and critically evaluate the impact of laws on the public.Cautioning the future civil servants about having to navigate new-age threats like information warfare, deepfakes, algorithmic bias, and climate justice, the prime minister instructed the recruitment agencies to adapt to these global shifts by prioritizing candidates' foresight and complex problem-solving abilities.He insisted that the examination agencies rapidly align with the nation's broader reform momentum by adopting the principle of time certainty to shorten exam cycles without lowering standards. These would cut down the financial burden on account of coaching fees, rent, and transport, on the families, he said.The prime minister proudly noted the dramatic rise in female candidates in civil services, from a mere 3% in 1952 to over 30%today, alongside the historic appointment of three out of four women UPSC chairpersons post-2014.Pointing to the 45-fold increase in candidate participation since the institution's 50th anniversary in 1976, Modi reminded the commissions that the recruiting agencies are not merely picking candidates, but choosing individuals who will become the very face and representative of the government at the grassroots level.Congratulating UPSC for having been in existence for 100 years, the prime minister praised the organisation's enduring credibility despite changing generations, governments, technologies, and syllabi. The celebrations were marked by the release of a commemorative postage stamp, a special coin, and a compilation of 100 significant case laws.Recalling the monumental challenges faced after independence, Modi paid deep homage to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel for establishing the vital steel frame required not just to keep the country independent, but to actively govern the newly formed nation. He acknowledged that while the UPSC has excellently discharged its historical duties, the focus must now decisively pivot toward the critical next 25 years that await the country.
Article Summary: Prime minister narendra modi asked recruitment agencies like union public service commission (upsc) to adopt selection parameters that not only test an aspirant's academic knowledge but also their motivation to join the civil services.modi, while addressing upsc's centenary celebrations here, explained that selecting individuals with the right inherent motivation makes it easier for the administration to adapt to rapidly changing public aspirations.

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not addressing rising inflation in his Mann Ki Baat radio address, accusing him of being “blissfully unconcerned” about the issue.The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat.“The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away. Vegetables are getting more expensive by the day, with onion prices soaring 48.27% in August. Items such as air conditioners, TVs and refrigerators are also set to become more expensive. Household savings are steadily declining, while family debt is mounting. In such a scenario, how is the common family supposed to meet its needs?” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X.Ramesh questioned why PM Modi continues to “sermonise” in the Mann Ki Baat series instead of addressing the public’s concerns.“In his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio series, the Prime Minister keeps sermonising on various issues, but when will he address the country’s most pressing concern—inflation? When will he care about the public’s worries? The public is already beleaguered by rising prices, and there’s no relief coming from the government.How on earth is the average family supposed to manage its budget? How long will the middle class and the poor have their backs broken like this?” the Rajya Sabha MP asked.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, retail inflation, based on the 2024=100 CPI, stood at 4.82% in August, up from 4.45% in July. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), rose to 5.95% in August from 5.52% in July. The August figures are provisional.Official data showed that onion inflation surged from 22.54% in July to 48.27% in August. Ginger recorded inflation of 73.82%, while garlic inflation stood at 43.60%. In contrast, tomato prices fell 31.09% year-on-year, while potato prices declined 13.14%.MoSPI data showed inflation in the combined food and beverages category at 5.66% in August. Transport inflation stood at 4.60 percent, education services at 3.73%, while restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 8.38%. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 15.17%.The CPI data was compiled from price information collected across 1,407 urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages nationwide. MoSPI reported a 100% response rate from both rural and urban markets in August.According to MoSPI, the next CPI data, covering September, is scheduled to be released on October 12.
Article Summary: Cong targets pm modi for 'ignoring' inflation in his mann ki baat radio address. Opposition party’s attack came a day after pm modi addressed the nation. Food inflation, measured by the consumer food price index (cfpi), rose to 5.95% in august.

Stock markets tumbled on Monday, with the benchmark Sensex plunging over 1,100 points to a six-month low and the Nifty closing below 22,800 as surging crude oil prices, geopolitical uncertainty and weak global trends weighed on investor sentiment.The 30-share BSE Sensex tanked 1,124.02 points, or 1.52 per cent, to settle at 72,771.72, its lowest closing level since March 30, 2026. During the session, it fell as much as 1,179.51 points, or 1.59 per cent, to 72,716.23.The market rout wiped out over Rs 6 lakh crore off the value of BSE-listed firms, whose combined market capitalisation stood at around Rs 476 lakh crore.Crude oil prices remained a key factor driving the benchmarks. Brent crude futures rose 1.5% to around $106 a barrel, while Asian markets declined 0.2%.Oil prices have remained volatile since late February, when the US and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran, triggering a war in the Middle East. Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have also continued for the seventh consecutive month. The latest rise in crude prices came amid a stalemate in US-Iran peace talks.Earlier, US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the confict.Meanwhile, Iran, maintained that diplomacy was the only way to resolve its conflict with the United States and Israel.The movement in crude prices remains particularly important for India, the world’s third-largest crude importer. A sustained rise in oil prices can raise the country’s import bill, fuel inflation and put pressure on corporate margins.Rupee also continues to face renewed pressure, falling 20 paise against US dollar as the greenback continues to see support.At the same time, foreign investor selling has also continued to weigh down domestic equities. Provisional data showed foreign investors were net sellers of Indian shares worth 36.94 billion rupees ($385.54 million) on Friday.Their selling in September has so far reached $1.8 billion, taking their total selling for the year to $25.86 billion."Globally, developments around US-Iran diplomacy and crude oil prices will remain critical. Any progress on a framework for reopening the Strait of Hormuz could ease energy prices and provide some relief to India's import bill and the rupee, while renewed geopolitical tensions could keep volatility elevated," Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research, Religare Broking, said.On the domestic front, Mishra said industrial production data for August and the HSBC manufacturing PMI reading would be released during the week. Market participants will also closely monitor foreign institutional investor (FII) activity and the upcoming monthly auto sales figures.Global bond yields are also expected to remain in focus following the Federal Reserve’s September policy decision.Ponmudi added that a series of economic data releases from the US would also be important for global risk sentiment. On the global front, US consumer confidence, JOLTS job openings and the eurozone’s September inflation cluster will be watched for signals on expectations around the global rate cycle.
